object_description: folded perimeter block with courtyard towers
design_condition: The folded block creates a sequence of context-specific squares and a lower-scaled ensemble that mediates between the surrounding urban fabric and internal campus spaces.

positive.statement: The folded block edge cleverly breaks down the scale of the large form.
The differentiated squares locate the building precisely in its heterogeneous context and create harmonious outdoor spaces.
The ground floor creates an innovative and robust sequence of public interior spaces with varied visual references.
The access and lounge areas ensure easy orientation and many meeting opportunities.
The project combines contextual openness with a strong architectural statement in one coherent building.
The spatial organization and room depths support flexible use.

negative.statement: The squares remain relatively schematic in their mood and materialization.
The central buildings appear anecdotal and compete with the geometry of the indented block.
The spatial concept and lighting would benefit from a quieter sequence of the central buildings.
The overall depth of the basement floors is problematic in relation to ground conditions.
The structural concepts and the integration of building services remain questionable.
The facade elements appear more like a formal gimmick than a comprehensible urban or programmatic expression.
The extensive glazing raises concerns about energy use and the targeted building standard.
Some delivery openings are considered too small.
